context_requirements: Proliferating cells with intact CDK/cyclin machinery and RB pathway
Expression of the targeted CDK(s) (e.g., CDK4/6 for G1 arrest; CDK1/2/9 for broader effects)
Functional p53 or p21 induction for robust transcriptional stress response
RB-proficient cells for G1 arrest; RB loss may shift response to G2/M or apoptosis
falsifiers: No decrease in proliferation-associated genes (e.g., CCNA2, CCNB1, MCM3, PCNA) at 24 h in any responsive line
No increase in CDKN1A or CDKN1B at 6 h or 24 h
No difference in transcriptional response between cell lines with intact versus defective RB or p53
Clear upregulation of proliferation genes at 24 h
No response in any of the nine cell lines

evidence.supports: p27Kip1 (CDKN1B) inhibits cyclin E-Cdk2 and links growth inhibitory signals to G1 arrest
p27 (CDKN1B) regulates proliferation and its expression has prognostic/therapeutic implications in cancer
p57KIP2 (CDKN1C) is a potent inhibitor of G1 cyclin/Cdk complexes and overexpression arrests cells in G1
HDAC1 loss elevates p21 and p27 and reduces cyclin-associated kinase activity, linking CDK inhibition to proliferation defects
p21WAF1/CIP1 is transcriptionally induced and its overexpression, like p27, causes cell-cycle exit/differentiation

changes: Removed PLK1, AURKA, AURKB, and BIRC5 from proximal_up: CDK inhibition does not directly induce these mitotic genes; they are typically downregulated with cell-cycle arrest.
Removed PLK1, AURKA, and BIRC5 from late_up for the same reason.
Removed CCNB1 from proximal_up because it also appears in proximal_down; a gene cannot be both up and down at the same time.
Kept CCNB1 only in proximal_down and late_down, consistent with CDK inhibitor-mediated G2/M arrest and reduced mitotic gene expression.
